highlight.text: The piece is also especially representative of English Romanticism in the nineteenth century as evidenced by spiritual presence of nature dominating the subject of the castle, as well as the rough brushstrokes enhancing this intensity.

Wikipedia: Hadleigh Castle is an oil painting by the English painter John Constable

work.text: At Hadleigh there is a ruin of a castle, which, from its situation, is vastly fine.
work.lead: On a sketching trip in Essex, fifteen years earlier:

source.author: John Constable
source.title: Letter to Maria Bicknell, 3 July 1814, in C. R. Leslie, Life and Letters of John Constable, R.A. (1896 ed.)

work.text: Constable visited Hadleigh Castle in 1814 and made a drawing of the castle. This he developed into a full-sized oil sketch in preparation for a finished painting, executed in 1829 and exhibited at the Royal Academy Exhibition of 1829.
I am in the height of agony about my crazy old walls of the Castle

source.author: John Constable
source.title: Note to C. R. Leslie, Hampstead, April 1829, in C. R. Leslie, Life and Letters of John Constable, R.A. (1896 ed.)

moment.text: The turmoil and distress of his mind is clearly seen in his later six-foot masterpieces Hadleigh Castle (1829) and Salisbury Cathedral from the Meadows (1831), which are amongst his most expressive pieces.
The "Hadleigh Castle," Constable's principal picture in the exhibition of 1829, received rather rougher usage than usual from the newspaper critics

source.author: C. R. Leslie
source.title: Life and Letters of John Constable, R.A. (1896 ed.)

matters.text: She was then on a sofa in their cheerful parlour, and although Constable appeared in his usual spirits in her presence, yet before I left the house he took me into another room, wrung my hand, and burst into tears, without speaking.
